note: Every question below gates a decision. 'what we have' and 'what we do not have' are separated on purpose: a decision made from the first column alone is a decision made from half the evidence. Where an answer exists it carries the official page that settles it.

rows.q: What is the current, official state of the league table?
rows.have: All 32 clubs, W/L/T, points for and against, and the split records, read from nfl.com on 2026-11-16. The table is internally consistent: wins equal losses at 148 each and points for equal points against at 6,880.
rows.missing: Nothing. This question is answered.
rows.answer: 32 clubs captured; the Monday-night fixture (LAC at BAL) had not kicked off, so 149 of 160 possible games are in the table.
rows.blocks: Any rating, any total, any line.
rows.discover: Re-read the official table after the Monday game and after every Sunday.

rows.q: Do the results we hold reproduce the official table exactly?
rows.have: A 7,240-game results feed with prices, and this session's transcription of the 12 Week-10 finals the feed snapshot predates.
rows.missing: Nothing for the reconciliation itself.
rows.answer: Yes: 32 of 32 clubs match the official W/L/T/PF/PA cell by cell.
rows.blocks: Trusting any backtest built on the feed.
rows.discover: Re-run console/verify.py; the reconciliation is recomputed from committed files.

rows.q: How stale is the results feed?
rows.have: The feed snapshot was taken 2026-11-15 13:21 UTC, before the Week 10 Sunday games: it holds 1 of 14 Week-10 results.
rows.missing: An automatic freshness alarm that fails the build when the feed is more than one game behind the official schedule.
rows.answer: Stale by 12 games as of this morning. Not an error — a snapshot taken before kickoff — but anything computed from it today is a Week-9-plus-Thursday model.
rows.blocks: Publishing ROI, CLV or any weekly number without a timestamp.
rows.discover: Compare max(gameday) in the feed with the last final on the official schedule page; fail loudly on a gap.

rows.q: Is the injury report we publish the one the league currently publishes?
rows.have: 347 rows across 28 clubs and 14 fixtures, captured 2026-11-15 and re-read 2026-11-16. The two reads are identical: sha256 9fe77d36...cd5f, 0 row differences, 0 field differences.
rows.missing: A clock time on each read (we hold a date only), and raw HTML (we hold rendered text).
rows.answer: Yes for content. The page has not changed in the 24 hours since the capture.
rows.blocks: Using the report as a forward-looking input after the games it describes have been played.
rows.discover: Capture Wednesday, Thursday and Friday with a timestamp; keep the raw bytes.

rows.q: Is the Week-10 report still forward-looking, or is it a post-game record?
rows.have: The page still shows Week 10 designations on the Monday after the games.
rows.missing: The official rule that says when a week's report is retired.
rows.answer: It is now a record of what was known before Week 10, not a forecast for Week 11. Any model that reads it as 'current' is reading last week's news.
rows.blocks: The injury feature in any Week-11 line.
rows.discover: Read the page daily at a fixed clock time; the first read that shows Week 11 is the boundary.

rows.q: Does any official source name the replacement for an injured starter?
rows.have: The league publishes dated starter changes for specific players (Drew Lock, Kyle McCord, Jacoby Brissett) in news articles, not in the injury table.
rows.missing: A structured, per-club field that names a replacement. There is none on the injury page.
rows.answer: No table exists; the evidence is article-shaped and player-by-player.
rows.blocks: B41 (per-team view) and B06 (depth of the replacement).
rows.discover: Capture the dated starter-change articles as they are published and store the URL per player.

rows.q: Can we rank a player's depth from anything official?
rows.have: Club depth pages for a subset of clubs; a 1st-to-6th string ladder for some.
rows.missing: All 32 clubs verified. Two clubs fail to parse: the Texans publish their chart as an image and the Packers prepend jersey numbers.
rows.answer: Not yet. 149 slots list more than one rank-1 player, so column one is not 'the starter'.
rows.blocks: B06, B45 (the deficiency matrix) and B52.
rows.discover: Verify the depth pages club by club, or capture official snap counts and derive the order from playing time.

rows.q: What does 'Questionable' actually mean?
rows.have: The official text publishes no percentage.
rows.missing: Any measured play rate per designation. We have never joined historical designations to the official inactive lists.
rows.answer: Unknown. Any percentage in the model today is borrowed from someone else's season.
rows.blocks: B44, B53, and any injury feature that uses a level rather than a change.
rows.discover: Join three or more seasons of designations to the official inactive lists and publish the play rate with an interval.

rows.q: Do we hold the opening price for any market?
rows.have: Closing spread, total and both moneylines with the price on each side, for 6,976 games.
rows.missing: Every opening number. The store is closing-only.
rows.answer: No. Closing-line value can be computed; opening-line movement cannot.
rows.blocks: B01, and any strategy that needs the move rather than the close.
rows.discover: Start writing an opening snapshot before the first move of each market.

rows.q: Is a parlay or prop combo rankable at all?
rows.have: The rule is written: a combo may be ranked only when a directly validated joint probability and the operator's void/push rules are both available.
rows.missing: Both. No joint probability has been validated and no operator rule text is stored.
rows.answer: No combo is rankable today. Multiplying marginals under dependence is invalid.
rows.blocks: B36, B37 (three of four leaderboard divisions) and any reward paid on a combo.
rows.discover: Validate a joint model on held-out data, and store the operator's void/push text verbatim.

rows.q: Has any strategy been registered before it saw the data?
rows.have: A registration ledger, a frozen shadow baseline and its Week-11 forecast.
rows.missing: Proof for every rule. Flag R26-01 records at least one commit (5a769b3) that carries a strategy's rule and its results together.
rows.answer: Not for all of them.
rows.blocks: B09, B67, B69, and any claim that the leaderboard is free of result-chasing.
rows.discover: For each rule, print the registration commit date and the first scored-result date; publish the gap.

rows.q: How large a sample separates skill from luck on this board?
rows.have: A power calculation on the committed sample: to detect a 1% win-probability edge needs about 17,689 bets; 2% needs 4,423; 3% needs 1,966; 5% needs 708.
rows.missing: A game-cluster adjustment, which is what independent bets really are not.
rows.answer: A season of a few hundred bets cannot distinguish a 2% edge from noise.
rows.blocks: Any promotion decision, and B38.
rows.discover: Publish a cluster-robust interval next to every ranking.

rows.q: Where is each fixture played, officially?
rows.have: A stadium column in the results feed, which is a parsed copy of the schedule, not an official transcription.
rows.missing: A venue transcribed from the official game centre for every fixture.
rows.answer: Not held. This is the one brief line with nothing behind it.
rows.blocks: B23, and the roof/surface overlay in B58.
rows.discover: Read each game-centre page and transcribe the venue; 14 reads for one week proves the method.

rows.q: Do we know the roof and the weather at kickoff?
rows.have: Roof, surface, temperature and wind per game from the schedule feed.
rows.missing: The official 90-minute roof designation, and any hourly forecast grid.
rows.answer: Half held. The historical column exists; the pre-game forecast does not.
rows.blocks: B58, and any total that is weather-sensitive.
rows.discover: Capture the dated roof designation and an NWS gridpoint forecast per game.

rows.q: Is 'not listed' the same as 'available'?
rows.have: 347 listed rows for 28 clubs.
rows.missing: The reserve lists. A player can be absent because he is on injured reserve, not because he is healthy.
rows.answer: No, and we cannot tell the difference today.
rows.blocks: B64, and every per-team injury count we print.
rows.discover: Capture the official reserve list per club and join it to the injury table.

rows.q: Who actually started, and who was actually inactive?
rows.have: 20 inactive rows for Week 9 only.
rows.missing: Official Game Books, inactive lists and snap counts for the current week.
rows.answer: Unknown. A backup starting for a starter can be suspected, not confirmed.
rows.discover: Capture the Game Book and the inactive list per game, then the snap counts.

rows.q: Are the depth rows we hold still true?
rows.have: A dated depth register.
rows.missing: The official transactions log, so staleness cannot be computed.
rows.answer: Unknown. At least one club publishes quarterbacks who are on injured reserve.
rows.discover: Capture the transactions log and flag every depth row older than the last roster event.

rows.q: Which club code is right, AZ or ARI, LA or LAR?
rows.have: nfl.com prints AZ for Arizona and LA for the Rams; the repository stores both conventions in different files.
rows.missing: A single mapping enforced at build time.
rows.answer: Open. Every join between files is exposed to it.
rows.blocks: Any cross-file join.
rows.discover: Fix one alias table and fail the build when a code is not in it.

rows.q: Do the scrapers fail loudly when a source changes?
rows.have: Field pins and freshness checks on most scrapers.
rows.missing: A row-count pin on the injury scraper. Two rows went missing in a 2026-11-14 scrape and nothing failed.
rows.answer: No, not on every scraper.
rows.blocks: B63, and the trustworthiness of every published count.
rows.discover: Pin the expected row count and the required fields per source; fail the build on any deviation.

rows.q: May we publish the raw rows we hold?
rows.have: Raw rows are published on the live site today.
rows.missing: A read of the data terms, and a decision recorded against them.
rows.answer: Undecided. An open pull request on this repository audits exactly this.
rows.blocks: B40, the public/private split.
rows.discover: Read the terms, record the decision, then move raw rows out of the Pages tree if the terms require it.

rows.q: Is the site itself reproducible and reachable?
rows.have: A single build command and a link checker; every page is reachable from the landing page.
rows.missing: Nothing material.
rows.answer: Yes. console/verify.py fails the build on a broken link, an empty cell or a row without an https source.
rows.blocks: Nothing.
rows.discover: Re-run the build and the checker after every change.

rows.q: What is the single number that would let us promote a strategy?
rows.have: Eight gates, including 200 scored bets, a real price on every bet, a holdout season, 60% of seasons positive, and a bootstrap interval that excludes zero.
rows.missing: A prospective sample. Every number on the board today is retrospective.
rows.answer: Nothing is promotable until a pre-registered strategy accumulates prospective bets that clear all eight gates.
rows.blocks: Any live staking, and B59.
rows.discover: Register one singles-only strategy, then record every prospective bet before kickoff and let the sample build.
